paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
model_annotation: The figure contains two side-by-side vertical bar charts illustrating inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss’ kappa) as a function of two ambiguity measures: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (left panel) and sample-level maximum ambiguity values (right panel). In both panels, the horizontal axis contains the category values: the left x-axis is labeled “Ambiguity Std” with four categories shown in left-to-right order (0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94), and the right x-axis is labeled “Max Ambiguity” with three categories shown in left-to-right order (1, 2, 3). The vertical axis in both panels is labeled “Fleiss Kappa” and uses a linear numeric scale with labeled ticks at approximately 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8, with the plotted values extending to just under 0.9. In the left panel, four single-series bars are shown in shades of blue: Ambiguity Std 0.0 (dark teal-blue) has a value labeled 0.88, 0.47 (medium blue) is labeled 0.46, 0.82 (light blue) is labeled 0.03, and 0.94 (brighter/light blue) is labeled 0.24. In the right panel, three single-series bars in similar blue shades are shown: Max Ambiguity 1 (dark teal-blue) is labeled 0.89, 2 (medium blue) is labeled 0.46, and 3 (light blue) is labeled 0.23. No legend is present, the bars are not stacked or grouped beyond the two separate panels, the category orders appear to follow the numeric x-axis values in each panel, and each bar is annotated with its numeric value above the bar without additional emphasis such as outlines or callouts.
